title: San Antonio group with Cordella, Bowman and Ayrton
summary: He worked about a year with Terry Shand, Charlie Cordella, Red Bowman and Sidney Ayrton; comments on where they are now.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: He played very good. What did he do? Go ahead. Well, I'll tell you. If you've heard, uh, William Manone, you'd probably— William Manone plays an authentic New Orleans style, and so did Leon Rapolo—I mean, Leon Prima in those days.

Would you call it, what they called goofus in those days, or would you call it, uh, like— We'd call it hot, hot trumpet. Hot trumpet, you'd call it. Yeah. Uh-huh. And that's what he was playing. Yeah. Um, did you ever know Charlie Cordella or Red Bowman or Sidney Ayrton?

Yes, I worked with all of them, too. Um, well, they were over in San Antonio. Worked in a little, uh, road spot, tavern, and, uh, there was Terry Shan and Charlie Cordella and Red Bowman and, uh, Sidney Ayrton, and they sent for me, and I went over to join them in San Antonio. And we worked together for, oh, a year or so, I guess. I've known Charlie ever since, Charlie Cordella, but I haven't seen him this trip. I understand he's still here in New Orleans.
That's right. So is Red, I believe.
Is he? Raymond Barton told me. He went, uh, down around Biloxi for a while. But I haven't seen, uh, either one, either Red Bowman or, uh, Charlie Cordella this trip.
How was Ayrton playing in those days?
